Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the UniInsure Holdings Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to UniInsure Holdings Inc.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Harper, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Financial Officer; David Kim, Chief Underwriting Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Investment Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Operating Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Claims Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Alex Harper.

Alex Harper: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on UniInsure Holdings Inc.'s performance for Q3. We delivered strong results, driven by robust premium growth, favorable changes in actuarial assumptions, expense ratio improvements from commission and operating efficiencies, declining customer acquisition costs, realized and unrealized investment gains, loss ratio enhancements via frequency and severity controls, a higher quarterly dividend, and accelerated share repurchases. Our commitment to innovation and customer service continues to drive our success.

Lisa Patel, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. As Alex mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $520 million, or $2.58 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included premium expansion, underwriting discipline, investment returns, cost efficiencies, claims management, and capital returns to shareholders. Our combined ratio was 92.1%. Investment income for the quarter was $680 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with our Risk-Based Capital ratio at 550%. Our expense ratio also improved to 26.8%.

Turning to our forward-looking guidance, I'd like to provide detailed insights on our premium growth outlook, which remains central to our strategy for profitable, sustainable expansion in the property & casualty and specialty lines markets. For the full year 2024, we are reaffirming our net written premium growth guidance of 7% to 9%, positioning us to reach approximately $28.5 billion to $29.2 billion in net written premiums, up from $26.6 billion in 2023. This includes organic growth of 6% to 8%, supplemented by the full-year impact of our recent acquisition of Midwest Specialty Risk Partners, contributing about 150 basis points in the second half.

For Q4 2024, we anticipate net written premium growth of 8% to 10% quarter-over-quarter, marking our strongest sequential growth in the past 18 months, aside from distortions from last year's California wildfire catastrophe losses affecting Q4 2023 retention. By segment, personal lines, which make up 45% of premiums, should see 9-11% growth in Q4 and 8-10% for the full year. Auto leads with telematics penetration at 32% of policies, up from 22% last year, powered by our DriveSafe AI program featuring real-time behavioral scoring on customer devices, driving 12% new business in usage-based insurance and improving loss ratios by 180 basis points via superior risk selection. Homeowners is on track for 7-9%, backed by 4.5% average rate hikes in non-cat exposed states, countering 6.2% year-over-year rebuild cost inflation per CoreLogic.

Commercial lines, 35% of premiums, guide to 6-8% growth for Q4 and the year, with small commercial middle-market renewals at 5.8% pricing, matching industry hardening. Workers' comp expanded 10% on payroll rebound and ESG products, while excess & surplus lines, now 18% of commercial, grew 15% as competitors like Chubb and Travelers retreated post-Hurricane Idalia, supported by 92.5% retention from our RiskForge machine learning platform for faster, accurate quoting.

Specialty and global, 20% of premiums, target 10-12% growth, propelled by cyber up 22% year-over-year amid ransomware events like Change Healthcare, with parametric triggers gaining via insurtech partnerships such as with Corvus. Our London platform aids international momentum.

Regionally, U.S. Southeast and Gulf Coast, 28% of the book, moderate to 5-7% in Q4 due to active Atlantic storms per NOAA's forecast of 17-25 named storms; we're non-renewing $450 million in high-risk Florida homeowners to hit a 95 combined ratio ex-cat, similar to Allstate's approach. Midwest and Northeast accelerate at 11-13%, with industrial de-risking boosting commercial demand. In Asia-Pacific, our 15% JV in UniInsure Asia mirrors AIG's model, adding 12% growth from motor and property via China's rebound and India's middle-class expansion, using RMS climate models for parametric flood pricing.

This guidance emphasizes profitable growth, with $1.2 billion in year-to-date rate actions yielding 4.2% net pricing after competition and California regulatory hurdles. Our cloud-native policy admin system has migrated 85% of policies to Guidewire Cloud, cutting quote-to-bind by 40% and lifting digital submissions 18%, with overall retention at 91.8% and expense leverage to 28.5%.

Risks encompass commercial rate softening projected at 5-7% in 2025 per Verisk, recession impacts on small businesses, or La Niña secondary perils. Yet our $4.8 billion deployable capital and 92% attritional combined ratio buffer M&A opportunities like Bermuda reinsurers for longevity transfer. Overall, this sets a mid-single-digit CAGR through 2026 with ROE to 14-15%, data-driven in a cycle favoring scaled incumbents.

Another significant factor was changes in our actuarial assumptions, netting a favorable $285 million pre-tax impact, or 24 basis points to our 92.1% combined ratio. Our Chief Actuary team recalibrates these quarterly using our Experience Studies database, enhanced by machine learning on 25 years of claims data, benchmarked to peers like Prudential, MetLife, and Chubb, following ASOP standards, VM-20 for life, and Solvency II for Europe.

Mortality and longevity drove $180 million favorable: Life & Annuity, 45% of our $180 billion in-force, shifted to a 2024 blended table from 2017 CSO, with U.S. A/E at 92% from vaccine and lifestyle gains in 50-70 cohorts. Annuities extended expectancy 0.3 years to 84.2 female/81.8 male per SOA Pri-2012, releasing $120 million reserves; UK/Canada milder at 0.1 year due to obesity. We hedge via Swiss Re longevity swaps on $5 billion at 4.2%.

Discount rates yielded $210 million: U.S. risk-free up 75 bps to 4.1% with 10-year Treasuries at 4.3%, discounting $40 billion P&C IBNR and $25 billion life liabilities for 52 bps margin gain. Europe IFRS 17 CSM unlocked €150 million ($162 million) as EIOPA curve rose 60 bps to 3.2%; Japan headwind of $25 million from 0.9% JGBs countered by $2 billion fixed annuity at 2.1% cap via ALM Monte Carlo hedging to 2040.

Morbidity, lapse, and expenses offset -$105 million: Group Benefits morbidity to 105% A/E from long COVID/mental health, adding $80 million on $10 billion book like Unum trends; auto lapses to 4.5% adding $15 million unearned; expenses up 1.5% for 3.2% wage inflation, $10 million hit; Australia bushfires added $20 million PML.

U.S. (70%) net $220 million favorable from cat-light ($450M vs. $650M budgeted) and telematics lapses; Europe (20%) $45 million from IFRS 17 despite French motor inflation; Asia (10%) -$20 million from Japan/China.

Ahead, $50 million in AI assumption governance with Milliman LLMs targets 5-10 bps volatility cut; $1.5 billion Munich Re quota share frees capital. Q4 unlocks $100-150 million at stable rates, combined ratio 91-93%, ROE 14%.

Our expense ratio improved to 26.8%, down 110 basis points year-over-year from 27.9% and 40 basis points sequentially, the sixth straight quarter of compression, trailing nine-month at 27.1% below our 27.5% target and AM Best's 28.6% P&C average, despite 4.2% input inflation and cat pressures on peers.

Commissions, 42% of underwriting expenses, fell to 11.3% of earned premiums, 60 bps better, shifting from 14-16% agent/broker to DTC/embedded at 6-8%. DTC auto/home now 32% U.S. personal lines vs. 24% ago, like Progressive telematics; Uber embedded rideshare $450 million annualized at sub-5%. North America 10.8%, down 90 bps; Europe 12.4% up 20 bps on MiFID II/broker M&A; Asia 11.1% down 150 bps via DBS bancassurance at 7-9%. FY2025 targets 50 bps more via AI agent portal cutting leakage 15-20%.

Operating costs to 15.5%, $180 million less on 8% growth via $750 million InsureTech 3.0 (22% ROI): claims STP 68% auto via Tractable-like vision AI, $145/claim cut; genAI underwriting 85% small commercial <2 min, $92 million Q3 save like Lemonade scaled; RPA/UiPath Manila 18% G&A, AWS 30% data cut.

U.S. 14.9% absorbing Helene cats; EMEA 16.8% GDPR/UK fees, €120 million OutSystems counter; APAC 15.2% India parametric via Planet Labs.

Q4 guides 26.5-26.7%, 30-50 bps better on 12% growth, combined 95.5%, mid-teens EPS.

Customer acquisition costs blended at $385 per new policy in Q3, down 8% sequentially from $418 and 18% year-over-year from $470, seventh straight quarter, trailing 12-month $405 vs. AM Best $520; peers $450-480, Lemonade sub-$350 narrower.

New PIF +28% YoY to 1.3 million, premium +22% $2.8 billion. Channel shift: digital 62% vs. 42%, DTC $290 vs. agents $620/brokers $780; Instant Quote telematics +24% conversions.

Paid media 35% ROI Google/Meta AI, CPC -22%, Amazon renters $210 CAC $15 billion market. $150 million tech: Salesforce/Guidewire -18 days cycles, commissions 14% vs. 22%; ML LTV 92% accuracy, 4.2x ratio >3.5 target.

U.S. $370 Sun Belt bundling; Europe $460 -12% YoY Aviva; APAC $520 Indonesia/India embeds.

Challenges: ad inflation countered SEO EV; broker +3% to hybrid digital. YE2024 sub-$360: embedded APIs, genAI chat 40% cut, 88% retention LTV +27%.

Investment results showed net realized gains $285 million, +15% QoQ from fixed/equity sales in $152 billion portfolio (40% pre-tax income). Unrealized loss $1.8 billion, +$450 million QoQ on 4.8% 10-year yield, excluded from core like Berkshire/MetLife.

Realized: $120 million tactical high-yield to munis; $95 million CLO upgrades AA; $70 million MBS to Treasuries, duration 5.1 years.

Unrealized AFS $110 billion: $650 million OTTI ($180 million earnings), $1.2 billion fixed, $450 million equities, +$150 million alts 9.1% IRR.

North America $1.1 billion loss corporates; Europe $200 million gain Bunds/gilts covered bonds; Asia flat JGB trim to infra.

Aladdin ALM 8% surplus shift; $25 billion HTM munis $420 million NII 4.2%; ESG $8 billion +25 bps; $10 billion swaps DV01 $15 million/10bps.

Q4 realized $300-350 million, NII $1.65-1.70 billion +12%, yield 4.8% AA-.

Loss ratio to 63.5% full-year, +170 bps, Q3 61.2% best since 2019 ex-cat via GLIDE.

Frequency: auto +2.8% 7.2/100 to miles +4.5% telematics; commercial flat 4.1/$1M exclusions; ex-cat -1.2% ML underwriting -12% rejects.

Severity +6.4% $18,200: auto $12,800 +9.2% parts/labor; workers flat $42,500 RTW; property +5.1% costs.

U.S. 64.1% 3.2 pts cat; Europe 58.7% milder weather; APAC 67.3% typhoons ceded 45%; LatAm 65% telematics.

GLIDE 85% intake -28% cycles +15% fraud $65 million; ApexDrive 42% -8% frequency; parametric hail.

2024 62-64% normalized cats, 6-8% pricing >4.5% trend.

On shareholder returns, our Board declared $0.82 quarterly dividend, +7.2% YoY/$0.765, sequential from $0.80, payable August 15 to July 31 record. 5-year CAGR 8.1% from $0.62, TTM $3.24 2.9% yield vs. Travelers 2.6%/Chubb 3.2%.

Payout 42% adj EPS $2.18 +11%, >2.3x core, FCF 1.8x $1.2 billion cash/$850 million NII 4.6%.

P&C 92.4% ex-45 pts cat underwriting $450 million +22%; Life IUL +28% $1.1 billion; Group MLR 82.1%.

U.S. auto 95.2% telematics; commercial 9% rates; Europe 91.8% UK motor; APAC +16% Japan/India offset Thailand cats.

Capital: organic/tech/M&A/$1.8 billion buybacks 4% float total 5.8%; RBC 580%; AI claims -35% cycles $200 million; ESG parametric +40%.

6-9% growth 3-5 years ROE 14.5%, hedge $28 billion 4.8% fixed/7.2% alts.

Share repurchases totaled $750 million Q3, 4.2 million shares at $178.57 average, +25% QoQ, YTD $2.3 billion 3.8% shares, 13 million retired to 285 million, +5 cents EPS.

Funded P&C/group $1.8 billion cash 8% premium 4.6% yield; opportunistic vs. M&A valuations; 10b5-1 VWAP 65% off-exchange 98% discount; AI cat pause.

U.S. 70% Florida/Texas hardening; EMEA $225 million Solvency II; APAC $150 million Japan.

$12.5 billion remaining $15 billion auth, 8-10% reduction, 12-15% IRR $22 billion surplus.

That covers our financial highlights.

David Kim: Thank you, Lisa. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our personal lines business. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophe risks and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including RiskForge analytics for machine learning-optimized quoting and dynamic pricing strategies tied to telematics and climate models, achieving 91.8% retention and 4.2% net pricing gains.

Robert Kline: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments in fixed income, munis, CLOs, and alternatives, with book yield at 4.8% and strong ALM hedging.

Tom Reilly: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including GLIDE AI for 68% STP auto claims and fraud detection saving $65 million annually. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times by 28%, lower cycle times, and improved claims resolution rates with 15% better fraud flagging.

Elena Vasquez: We are making significant investments in technology to enhance our operations and improve the customer experience. Our new Guidewire Cloud policy administration system, along with genAI underwriting and claims platforms like Vertex AI and Tractable vision, is expected to drive significant efficiencies and cost savings, with quote-to-bind down 40% and sales cycles reduced 18 days.

Maria Gonzalez: As COO, I've overseen the operational integration of these tech initiatives and the Midwest acquisition, ensuring smooth scaling across regions while maintaining our efficient growth framework.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the premium growth guidance for next quarter and the full year?

Alex Harper: Good morning, John. Absolutely, as Lisa detailed, we're reaffirming 7-9% full-year growth to $28.5-29.2 billion, with Q4 at 8-10% sequential. Personal lines 9-11% led by auto telematics at 32% penetration and DriveSafe AI; commercial 6-8% with E&S 15%; specialty 10-12% cyber tailwinds. Regional moderation in Gulf Coast offset by Midwest/Northeast strength and Asia JV 12%. Profitable focus with $1.2 billion rates and 91.8% retention.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of rising interest rates on your business?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, Emily. Higher rates are a tailwind, boosting investment income to $680 million at 4.8% yield, with $210 million favorable discount rate unlocks on reserves and NII growth 12%. ALM hedges cap DV01 at $15 million/10 bps, and reinsurance quota shares free capital. Actuarial gains $285 million including 75 bps U.S. risk-free lift. We expect stabilization supporting Q4 realized gains $300-350 million.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez: What is the expected impact of potential regulatory changes in catastrophe-exposed states on your underwriting strategy?

David Kim: Good morning, Mike. In states like California and Florida, we're proactively non-renewing $450 million high-risk to target 95 ex-cat combined, echoing peers. Pricing discipline with 6-8% filings across 75% book outpaces trends, backed by RiskForge ML for selection. Regulatory pushback post-Prop 103 managed within 4.2% net gains.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Bennett with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Laura Bennett: Can you elaborate on the expected benefits of the new technology platform?

Elena Vasquez: Good morning, Laura. Guidewire Cloud and InsureTech 3.0 deliver 22% ROI: 85% small commercial underwrites <2 min, claims STP 68% saving $145/claim, RPA 18% G&A. Digital submissions +18%, CAC payback <9 months, enabling 32% DTC shift and LTV 4.2x. Further genAI pilots target 40% CAC cut.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Lee with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

David Lee: Thanks. On loss ratio drivers, how are you addressing severity inflation?

Tom Reilly: Good morning, David. Severity up 6.4% to $18,200, auto parts/labor key, but workers flat via RTW, property via dynamic deductibles. GLIDE flags fraud, telematics -8% frequency high-risk; parametric pilots with Munich Re. Expects 62-64% 2024 normalized cats.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] That covers our questions for now.

Alex Harper: Thank you for your questions and your interest in UniInsure Holdings Inc. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
